report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Parsing pyproject, disk packages, bytecode orphans; cleaning annotations; harvesting old inventory; building feature entries.

symbols.name: _packages_on_disk
symbols.note: Walks distribution roots from listed package names; collects dotted packages with __init__.py; skips _STALE_SKIP_DIRS and dot-dirs; returns sorted unique relative dotted paths.

symbols.name: _orphan_bytecode
symbols.note: Walks tree; finds __pycache__ dirs with .pyc but no sibling .py; returns sorted (relative_path, pyc_count) tuples.

symbols.name: _clean_annotation
symbols.note: Filters a mapping to allowed keys with non-empty stripped string values; returns dict.

symbols.name: annotation_overreach
symbols.note: Given a mapping of annotations, reports keys whose values are not mappings or contain fields outside the human-allowed set; returns list of strings.

symbols.name: _module_targets
symbols.note: Resolves entrypoint tokens to known module paths; handles dotted names by trying .py and /__init__.py; returns unique hits in order.

symbols.name: harvest
symbols.note: Extracts annotations and narrative features from old inventory; handles schema-2 pass-through and legacy areas/env_vars; merges multiple annotations per module with ' | '.

symbols.name: _feature
symbols.note: Builds a feature dict from facts, entry identifiers, dark switches, and annotation; merges human fields.

symbols.name: _stale_features
symbols.note: Computes ghost packages, gaps, and orphan bytecode; builds stale feature dicts with annotations.

claims.text: Dotted packages that exist under the distribution roots the metadata already names. Scoped to those roots on purpose: every directory in the repo with an ``__init__.py`` is not a candidate for the wheel, and treating a fixture or a runs/ directory as one would manufacture findings.
claims.why: The function only walks directories under root/top where top is the first component of a listed package; it checks __init__.py and skips _STALE_SKIP_DIRS and dot-dirs; it returns only those relative paths.

claims.text: ``__pycache__`` directories holding bytecode whose sources are gone.
claims.why: The function walks, finds __pycache__ dirs, checks for .pyc files, and only includes those whose parent has no .py siblings.

claims.text: The exact shape of the ``daedalus/hermes`` remnant the hand-written inventory recorded: the package was deleted, the ``.pyc`` files stayed, and an import of the dotted name could still resolve. A cache beside live sources is not a finding -- only one with NO sibling ``.py`` at all.
claims.why: It checks parent directory for any .py files; if any exist, it skips. Only orphan caches (no sibling .py) are returned.

claims.text: Annotation keys carrying fields a human is NOT allowed to set.
claims.why: It computes allowed fields from FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS, ENV_HUMAN_FIELDS, AREA_HUMAN_FIELDS; for each annotation value, if not a mapping it reports 'not an object', else reports extra keys.

claims.text: Reported rather than silently dropped. Silently dropping is how a person concludes the field works; naming it is how they learn the rule.
claims.why: The function builds a list of strings describing each offending key and returns it; it does not modify the annotations.

claims.text: The build ignores these fields either way -- an annotation that could set ``status`` would hand the hand-written file's exact power back through a side door.
claims.why: The claim about how the build ignores these fields is not verifiable in this chunk; the build logic is in later functions not shown here.

claims.text: Every module a hand-written feature's entrypoints resolve to.
claims.why: The function iterates over all entrypoints and all tokens, collecting all matching known modules, not just the first.

claims.text: ALL of them, not the first: the kairos-rename shim entry names five modules in one feature, and attaching its rationale to only one of them would lose the reason for the other four.
claims.why: The loop appends every unique hit to `hits`; it does not stop at the first.

claims.text: Lift the human half out of a previous inventory. LOSSLESS by contract.
claims.why: The function attempts to put every feature either into annotations or narrative; it counts matched and narrative, and for schema-2 it passes blocks through. It does not drop features except when they are not mappings or have no human fields; but the docstring's lossless claim is supported by the explicit narrative fallback for features without targets.

claims.text: Returns ``(annotations, narrative_features, stats)``. Every feature in the old document ends up in exactly one of the two: an annotation keyed to the module(s) its entrypoints name, or a verbatim narrative feature. Nothing is dropped, because a generated file that discards the rationale somebody wrote is not progress -- it is the same rot with a fresher timestamp.
claims.why: For legacy areas, features with no targets go to narrative verbatim; features with targets go to annotations. For schema-2, annotations and narrative_features are copied. However, note that a feature with targets but no human fields still gets an annotation entry with empty dict, which is not dropped. Also, features with targets are not kept verbatim in narrative, but the docstring says 'exactly one of the two' -- that is satisfied.

claims.text: Already-schema-2 documents pass their blocks straight through; the harvest only has work to do the first time.
claims.why: If old.get('schema') == SCHEMA, it copies annotations and narrative_features and returns immediately, only counting them.

claims.text: The two mechanically-detectable kinds of staleness, plus the packaging picture they come from.
claims.why: The function computes ghosts (listed but not on disk) and gaps (on disk but not listed), plus orphans from _orphan_bytecode. It builds features for ghosts (and presumably gaps and orphans in the rest of the function, which is cut off but the docstring is consistent with the visible part).

claims.text: Deliberately only two. "This directory is a superseded experiment" and "this mockup was replaced by the shipped app" are judgements about intent, and a scanner that guessed at them would fill the work queue with its own guesses. They stay in ``narrative_features``, where a human signed them.
claims.why: The visible portion of _stale_features only shows the ghost-package loop; the rest of the function (gaps, orphans, and how narrative_features are handled) is not in this chunk. The claim about narrative_features staying for human-signed items cannot be fully verified here.

claims.text: Two hand-written features naming one module. Both reasons are kept, joined, rather than one silently winning.
claims.why: In the annotations merge loop, when an existing annotation exists, each human field is merged: if prior is empty it is set; otherwise if the new value is not already in prior, it is joined with ' | '.

observations.what: _stale_features docstring says 'The two mechanically-detectable kinds of staleness' but the function computes three categories: ghosts, gaps, and orphans. The docstring may refer to ghosts and gaps as the two kinds, with orphans as a separate packaging picture, but the phrasing is ambiguous.

_orphan_bytecode uses os.walk and modifies dirnames in place to skip _STALE_SKIP_DIRS, but does not skip dot-directories like the _packages_on_disk function does. This could lead to scanning .hidden __pycache__ directories, but that is likely harmless.

In _module_targets, the token regex _TOKEN_RE is not defined in this chunk; its behavior is assumed to extract path-like tokens. If it does not handle certain formats, the resolution could miss modules, but that is uncheckable here.

harvest for schema-2 documents copies annotations and narrative_features but does not validate that the annotations are cleaned or that narrative features are dicts; it only filters narrative to Mappings. This could allow non-human fields to pass through, but the docstring says 'pass their blocks straight through', which is consistent.

risks: _stale_features docstring | low | The docstring claims 'two mechanically-detectable kinds' but the function computes three (ghosts, gaps, orphans); could mislead readers about what is detected. | Read the rest of _stale_features to see if gaps and orphans are presented as part of the packaging picture rather than as staleness kinds.

_orphan_bytecode | low | Does not skip dot-directories when walking, unlike _packages_on_disk; could scan hidden __pycache__ dirs, but likely harmless. | Check if _STALE_SKIP_DIRS includes dot-dirs or if the walk should also skip dot-dirs.

_module_targets | medium | The token regex is external to this chunk; if it doesn't capture certain entrypoint formats, module resolution could be incomplete. | Inspect _TOKEN_RE definition elsewhere in the file.

harvest schema-2 | low | Passes annotation blocks through without cleaning; could allow non-human fields to persist, but docstring says 'straight through'. | Verify whether the build later ignores non-human fields anyway.
